title: A Child Session names its Parent in a telemetry attribute

statements.says: The driver passes the starting Session's ID to each Session it starts, as skillworks.parent.session.id in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES.
The Sessions list shows the Parent alone, with its Children's Measures added in.
A Session that names no Parent is never a Child, so a chat, a single /implement and a claude -p started by hand keep their own rows.
A driver started by hand from a terminal has no Parent to name, and its Sessions show one by one, as they did before.
The driver adds its key to any OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES it was given, and never replaces what is there.
The SessionStart and Load records written by the hook carry the same key.
The link is one level deep on purpose: a Session a Child starts names the first Parent too.
The driver starts every step as its own claude -p, so one spec run lands in the Sessions list as dozens of rows that make no sense apart.
Claude Code hands the Session's ID to every command it runs as CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID.
Claude Code puts every key from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES on every event it sends, so each event of a Child names its Parent.
The Parent is a real Session, so its name, start, Cost and Running state already exist.
The hook's records carry the key because otherwise a Child's own records would still reach the list without it.
A made-up row for the spec was rejected, because that row is not a Session and Studio would have to invent its name, start, Cost and Running state.

One shared trace as the link was rejected, because a trace ID names nothing and one trace for a run of many hours grows very large; it does not conflict with the attribute, and a later view of the whole run may still use it.
